> **How to read this.** First full `semantic_type` benchmark: the cheap pair on 478 chunks from 30 mock postings (written by Claude, labeled by Sonnet and Opus). "agreed" is Opus's label where the two disagree; "adjudicated" is "agreed" with 8 reviewed corrections (section labels and banners that both labelers had labeled by the section they introduce; see `backend/evals/data/labels/adjudications.json`). The two models are not significantly different on either label set; the ranking flips between them. `jev-1.14.0` pricing is unverified. Run history: 80 calls were repeats (`--repeats 2` on 40 items), and 164 of `gpt-5.4-mini`'s calls were retried after Azure rate limiting, so its cost line includes those extra calls.

# Eval report: semantic_type

478 items. Quality is against each label source separately, on each item's first run; an item whose model gave an invalid answer counts as wrong. Items with no answer because of rate limits or connection errors are excluded, not wrong. Per-class, confusion and calibration tables use the **adjudicated** labels.

| model | coverage | no answer | acc vs adjudicated | acc vs agreed | acc vs silver:opus-5-5 | acc vs silver:sonnet-5-5 | macro-F1 (adjudicated) | ECE | p50 ms | p95 ms | $/1k items | errors | retried | consistency |

Accuracy shows the 95% Wilson interval. ECE is expected calibration error on the top-class probability (n/a where a model reports none).

## Pairwise (exact McNemar)

- vs agreed labels: gpt-5.4-mini vs jev-1.14.0 on 478 items: only gpt-5.4-mini right on 12, only jev-1.14.0 right on 4; p = 0.077 (no significant difference)
- vs adjudicated labels: gpt-5.4-mini vs jev-1.14.0 on 478 items: only gpt-5.4-mini right on 5, only jev-1.14.0 right on 11; p = 0.210 (no significant difference)
